is_anopheles.evidence: This study evaluated the effects of temperature on the susceptibility of Anopheles gambiae sensu lato (s.l.) mosquitoes to pyrethroids and their expression of metabolic enzymes (p. 1, Abstract).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The study performed species identification PCR (An. gambiae s.s. and An. coluzzii) and biochemical enzyme assays (MFO, GST, alpha/beta esterase), but did not genotype any target resistance markers such as Vgsc or Ace-1.

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: No target resistance marker genotyping was performed, so no genotype counts or frequencies are reported.

african_field_population.evidence: The study tested laboratory-established colonies (Tiassalé and Kisumu strains) maintained in an insectary at the Vestergaard-Noguchi Memorial Institute for Medical Research Vector Labs (p. 3, 'Mosquito colony'). No field-collected mosquitoes were used.

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a primary laboratory experimental study examining rearing temperature, bioassay mortality, and metabolic enzyme levels.

sub_country_location.evidence: No field collection sites are reported as laboratory colony strains were used.

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: No field collection timeframe is reported as laboratory colony strains were used.

duplicate_risk.evidence: Laboratory colony study; no field sample overlap.

supplement.evidence: Supplementary files were not needed because the main text confirms no target resistance markers were genotyped.

assessment.summary: This laboratory experiment evaluated the impact of rearing temperature (25 to 40 °C) on pyrethroid susceptibility (WHO tube tests using deltamethrin and permethrin) and metabolic enzyme expression (MFO, GST, alpha- and beta-esterase) in laboratory colonies of Anopheles gambiae s.l. (Tiassalé and Kisumu strains). The study did not genotype target insecticide-resistance markers and did not evaluate African field populations.
